questions.q: If the equation& $x^{2} + bx + 45 = 0, b \in R$ has conjugate complex roots and they satisfy \left|z + 1\right| = 2\sqrt{10},$ then$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $z = \alpha + i\beta$ be~one of the roots of the equation $x^{2} + bx + 45 = 0, b \in R$.

So, its other conjugate complex root will be~$z = \overset{¯}{\alpha + i\beta} = \alpha - i\beta$.

We know that for a quadratic equation~$Ax^{2} + Bx + C = 0$, the sum and product of its roots are~$- \dfrac{B}{A} \text{ and } \dfrac{C}{A}$~respectively.

So, the sum of roots of the given equation,~\left(\alpha + i\beta\right) + \left(\alpha --i\beta\right) = - $\dfrac{b}{1}⇒ $2\alpha = -$b . . . . . . \left($i\right)$.

Also, the product of roots of the given equation, \left(\alpha ++i\beta\right) \left(\alpha - i\beta\right) = $\dfrac{45}{1}$⇒ {α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = 45 . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$.

Now, given that~\left|z + 1\right| = $2\sqrt{10}.

$⇒ \left|\alpha \pm i\beta + 1\right| = $2\sqrt{10}

$⇒ $\sqrt{\left(\alpha + 1\right)2 + {β}^{2}} =2\sqrt{10}

$⇒ \left(\alpha +1\right)2 + {β}^{2} = 40 . . . . . . \left(iii\right)$

Subtracting equation~ \left(ii\right)$~from equation~ \left(iii\right)$, we get

\left(\alpha +1\right)2 - {α}^{2} = - 5$

$⇒ \left(\alpha +1 + \alpha\right) \left(\alpha +$1 - $\alpha\right) = -$5$~ \left[∵ a^{2} - b^{2} = \left(a + b\$right)\left($a - b\right)\right]$

$⇒ $2\alpha +$1 = - 5$

$⇒ $2\alpha = -$6$

Comparing from equation~ \left(i\right)$, we get

$b = 6$

$∴ b^{2} - b = {6}^{2} - 6 = 36 - 6 = 30$.

Also,~$b^{2} + b = {6}^{2} + 6 = 36 + 6 = 42$.

Hence, option~ \left($a\right)$& is correct.

questions.q: Let for some real numbers $\alpha$~and $\beta, a = \alpha - i\beta$. If the system of equations $4ix + \left(1 + i\right)y = 0$~and~$8\left(cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + isin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)x + \overset{¯}{a}y = 0$~has more than one solution then $\dfrac{α}{β}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given system of equations has more than one solution, then it must have infinitely many solutions.

So,& $\dfrac{4i}{8\left(cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + isin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)} = \dfrac{1 + i}{\alpha + i\beta}$~ \left(∵ \begin{cases}a & = \alpha - i\beta \\ ⇒ a & = \alpha + i\beta\end{cases}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{4i}{8\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2} + i\dfrac{3}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1 + i}{\alpha + i\beta}$

$⇒ \alphai - \beta = - 1 - i + \sqrt{3}i - \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ - \beta + \alphai = \left(- 1 - \sqrt{3}\right) + \left(- 1 + \sqrt{3}\right)i$

$⇒ \alpha = - 1 + \sqrt{3}$~&~$- \beta = - 1 - \sqrt{3}$

$∴ \dfrac{α}{β} = \dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{3}}{1 + \sqrt{3}}= \dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{3}}{1 + \sqrt{3}} \times \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{3}}{1 - \sqrt{3}}$

$= \dfrac{- \left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right)2}{1 - 3} = \dfrac{1 + 3 - 2\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2 - \sqrt{3}$

$

questions.q: If $z = \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{i}{2}\left(i = \sqrt{- 1}\right),$ then ${\left(1 + iz + z^{5} + iz^{8}\right)}^{9}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$z = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{i}{2} ∴ iz = - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i = \omega$
$∴ {\left(1 + iz + z^{5} + iz^{8}\right)}^{9} = {\left(1 + \omega + \dfrac{{\omega}^{5}}{i^{5}} + i \times \dfrac{{\omega}^{8}}{i^{8}}\right)}^{9}$
$= {\left(1 + \omega - i{\omega}^{2} + i{\omega}^{2}\right)}^{9}$
$= {\left(- {\omega}^{2}\right)}^{9} = - {\omega}^{18}$
$= - 1$

questions.q: Let $p, q \in \mathbb{R}$ and~$( 1 - \sqrt{3}i{)}^{200} = {2}^{199} ( p + iq )$,~$i = \sqrt{- 1}$. Then,~$p + q + q^{2}$~and~$p - q + q^{2}$& are roots of the equation.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$( 1 - \sqrt{3}i{)}^{200} = {2}^{199} ( p + iq )$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3}{2}i\right)200 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left($p + iq\right)$

$⇒ \left(cos \$left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) -isin \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right)\right)200 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left($p + iq\right)$

$⇒ \left(cos \left(\dfrac{200\pi}{3}\right) -isin $\$left(\dfrac{200\pi}{3}\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(p + iq\right)$

$⇒ $\l$left(cos\l$left(201\pi - $\dfrac{π}{3}\right) -isin \$lleft(201\pi - \dfrac{π}{3}\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \left($p + iq\right)$

$⇒ \left(-$cos \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) -$isin \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(p + iq\right)$

$⇒ 2\left(- \dfrac{1}{2} - i\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = p + iq$

$⇒ - 1 - i\sqrt{3} = p + iq$

So,

$p = - 1, q = - \sqrt{3}$

$\alpha = p + q + q^{2} = 2 - \sqrt{3}$

$\beta = p - q + q^{2} = 2 + \sqrt{3}$

So,

$\alpha + \beta = 4$

$\alpha \cdot \beta = 1$

Required equation is

$x^{2} - 4x + 1 = 0

$

questions.q: Let $\alpha = \dfrac{- 1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}$. If $a = \left(1 + \alpha\right)\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{100}{\alpha}^{2k}$ and $b = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{100}{α}^{3k}$, then $a$ and $b$, are the roots of the quadratic equation.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\alpha = \dfrac{- 1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$a = \left(1 + \alpha\right)\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{100}{\alpha}^{2k}$ and

$b = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{100}{α}^{3k}$

Now

$\alpha = \omega; \omega = \dfrac{- 1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}$

Using this~$a$~and~$b$~can be written as~
$a = \left(1 + \omega\right) \left($1 + ${\omega}^{2} + {\omega}^{4} + \ldots {\omega}^{198} + {\omega}^{200}\right)
$= \left($1 + $\omega\right)\dfrac{\left(1 - {\left({\omega}^{2}\right)}^{101}\right)}{1 - {\omega}^{2}} = \dfrac{\left(1 + \omega\right)\left(1 - \omega\right)}{1 - {\omega}^{2}} =$1$

Similarly,

$b = 1 + {ω}^{3} + {ω}^{6} + \ldots + {ω}^{300} = 101$
So, the required quadratic equation is~

$x^{2} - \left($a + b\right)x + ab = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} - 102x + 101 = 0$.

$

questions.q: If $z = x + iy, xy \ne 0$, satisfies the equation ${z}^{2} + i\overset{¯}{z} = 0$, then $\left|{z}^{2}\right|$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: ${z}^{2} + i z = 0$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = - i z$

Now taking $z = x + iy$ we get,

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2ixy = - ix - y$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} = - y \text{ and } 2xy = - x$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} = - y \text{ and } x\left(2y + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)}^{2} = - \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

Hence, $z = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + i\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} \pm 2i\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \pm i\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left|{z}^{2}\right| = {\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}}\right)}^{2} = 1$
questions.question: If $z = x + iy, xy \ne 0$, satisfies the equation ${z}^{2} + i\overset{¯}{z} = 0$, then $\left|{z}^{2}\right|$ is equal to :
questions.explanation:
Given: ${z}^{2} + i z = 0$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = - i z$

Now taking $z = x + iy$ we get,

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2ixy = - ix - y$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} = - y \text{ and } 2xy = - x$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} = - y \text{ and } x\left(2y + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)}^{2} = - \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

Hence, $z = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + i\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} \pm 2i\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \pm i\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left|{z}^{2}\right| = {\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}}\right)}^{2} = 1$

questions.q:
If $z$ and $\omega$ are two complex numbers such that~\left|z\omega\right| = 1$ and $arg\left(z\right) - arg\left(\omega\right) = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, then~$arg \left(\dfrac{1 - 2\overset{¯}{z}\omega}{1 + 3\overset{¯}{z}\omega}\right) is:
(Here $arg \left(z\right)$ denotes the principal argument of complex number $z)$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
As

\left|z\omega\right| = 1$

If \left|z\right| = r$, then \left|\omega\right| = \dfrac{1}{r}$

Let $arg \left($z\right) = $\theta

$∴ arg\left(\omega\right) = \left(\theta - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)

So,

$z = re^{i$\theta}$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{z} = re^{i \left(- \theta\right)}$
$⇒ $\omega = \dfrac{1}{r}$e^{i \left(\theta - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)}$

Now, consider
\dfrac{1 - 2\overset{¯}{z}\omega}{1 + 3\overset{¯}{z}\omega} = \dfrac{1 - 2e^{i \left(- $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)}}{1 + 3e^{i \left(- $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)}} = \left(\dfrac{1 - 2i}{1 + 3i}\right)$

$= \dfrac{ \left($1 - 2i\right)\left(1 - 3i\right)}${ \left($1 + 3i\right) \left($1 - 3i\right)} = \dfrac{1 - 5i + 6i^{2}}{10} = \dfrac{- 5 + 5i}{10} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left($1 + i\right)$

Then,

$principalarg \left(\dfrac{1 - 2\overset{¯}{z}\omega}{1 + 3\overset{¯}{z}\omega}\right)

$= principalarg \left(- \dfrac{1}{2} \left($1 + i\right)\right)$

$= - \left(\pi - $\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{- 3\pi}{4}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $arg\left(\dfrac{3{z}_{1}}{2{z}_{2}}\right) = \theta,$~and we know that, if the~$arg\left(z\right) = \alpha,$~then~$arg\left(\dfrac{1}{z}\right) = - \alpha .$

$∴ z = \dfrac{3}{2}\left|\dfrac{z1}{z2}\right| \left($cos$\theta +$isin$\theta\right) + \dfrac{2}{3}\left|\dfrac{z2}{z1}\right|\left($cos$\theta -$isin$\theta\right)

Given,~$3\left|{z}_{1}\right| =$4\left|{z}_{2}\right|,$⇒ \left|\dfrac{z1}{z2}\right| = \dfrac{4}{3},

$⇒ z = $\dfrac{3}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{3} \lleft(cos\theta ++isin\theta\right) + \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{3}{4}\l$lleft(cos\theta -$-isin\theta\right)$

$⇒ z = 2 \l$left(cos\theta +$+isin\theta\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\l$left(cos\theta -$-isin\theta\right)

$⇒ z = $\d$dfrac{5}{2}cos\theta + \left(\d$dfrac{3}{2}sin\theta\right)$i$

$∴ \left|$z\right| = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4}\cos^{2}\theta + \dfrac{9}{4}\sin^{2}\theta}$

Now, using~\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta =$1,$~we get

\left|$z\right| = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4}\cos^{2}\theta + \dfrac{9}{4}\left(1 - \cos^{2}\theta\right)}$

$⇒ \left|$z\right| = \sqrt{4\cos^{2}\theta + \dfrac{9}{4}}$

And, we know that the maximum value of~cos\theta~is~$1 .$
$∴ \left|$z\right|max = \sqrt{4 + \dfrac{9}{4}} = \dfrac{5}{2} .$

$

$⇒ \left({z}_{2} + \left|{z}_{2} - 1\right|\right)\left(\overset{¯}{z}2 + \left|{z}_{2} - 1\right|\right) = \left({z}_{2} - \left|{z}_{2} +$1\right|\right)\left(\overset{¯}{z}2 - \left|{z}_{2} +1\right|\right)$

$⇒ \left({z}_{2} + \overset{¯}{z}2\right) \left( \left|{z}_{2} +1\right| + \left|{z}_{2} -1\right|\right) = 2\left({z}_{2} + \overset{¯}{z}2\right)$

$⇒$ Either ${z}_{2} + \overset{¯}{z}2 = 0$ or \left|{z}_{2} +1\right| + \left|{z}_{2} -1\right| = 2$

i.e.~${z}_{2}$~lies on imaginary axis or it lies on the line segment joining~ \left(-$1, 0\right)$~and~ \left($1, 0\right)$

Hence,~\left|{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|$min = \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2} - \sqrt{6}x + 3 = 0$ such that $Im ( \alpha ) > Im ( \beta )$. Let $a, b$ be integers not divisible by $3$and $n$ be a natural number such that $\dfrac{\alpha99}{β} + {α}^{98} = {3}^{n} ( a + ib ) , i = \sqrt{- 1}$. Then $n + a + b$ is equal to ___________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x^{2} - \sqrt{6}x + 3 = 0$ has roots $\alpha & \beta$

Now, solving $x^{2} - \sqrt{6}x + 3 = 0$ we get,

$x = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} \pm i\sqrt{6}}{2} = \sqrt{3} \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \pm \dfrac{1}{2}i\right)$

Now, taking $\alpha = \sqrt{3} \left(e^{i\dfrac{π}{4}}\right), \beta = \sqrt{3}\left(e^{- i\dfrac{π}{4}}\right)$

Now, solving $\dfrac{\alpha99}{β} + {α}^{98} = {α}^{98} \left(\dfrac{α}{β} +1\right)$

$= \dfrac{{α}^{98} ( \alpha + \beta )}{β}$

$= \dfrac{{3}^{49}\left(e^{i\dfrac{π}{4}}\right)98\left(\sqrt{6}\right)}{\sqrt{3} \left(e^{- i\dfrac{π}{4}}\right)}$

$= ${3}^{49}\$lleft(e^{i99\dfrac{π}{4}}\right)\times \sqrt{2}$

$= ${3}^{49}\$lleft(cos\dfrac{99\pi}{4} +++isin\dfrac{99\pi}{4}\right) \times \sqrt{2}

$= ${3}^{49}\l$left(cos\lleft(25\pi - $\dfrac{π}{4}\right) ++$isin\lleft(25\pi - $\dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right) \times \sqrt{2}

$= {3}^{49} ( - 1 + i )$

$= {3}^{n} ( a + ib )$

So, on comparing we get,

$n = 49, a = - 1, b = 1$

$∴ n + a + b = 49 - 1 + 1 = 49$

$

questions.q: The least positive integer $n$ such that $\dfrac{( 2i{)}^{n}}{( 1 - i{)}^{n - 2}}, i = \sqrt{- 1},$& is a positive integer, is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{( 2i{)}^{n}}{( 1 - i{)}^{n - 2}}$

$= \dfrac{( 2i{)}^{n}}{( - 2i) \dfrac{n - 2}{2}}$

$= \dfrac{( 2i{)}^{\dfrac{n + 2}{2}}}{( - 1{)}^{\dfrac{n - 2}{2}}}$

$= \dfrac{\left(2\right)\dfrac{n + 2}{2}i\dfrac{n + 2}{2}}{( - 1) \dfrac{n - 2}{2}}$
Clearly $n$~must be even $n = 2, 4$~rejected.~

So the least positive integer possible is~$n = 6$
